body:
did you know: the girl in "august" almost had a name.

she's the third narrator of folklore's teenage love triangle -- the summer that "slipped away" -- and she is never once named in the lyrics. it was in the long pond sessions that taylor mused the character might be "augusta. or augustine." fans took that and made it canon.

taylor wrote and produced her with jack antonoff as the triangle's sympathetic wildcard: the girl who deserved kindness, not blame, for a romance that was never really hers. "august" entered the hot 100 at no. 23 in the album's opening week, and that outro -- the full-orchestra major-chord climax -- is the biggest purely musical moment on the record. rob sheffield later ranked it fifth in her entire catalog, "the album's most plainly beautiful ballad."

happy salt-air month. the girl who slipped away has a whole one named after her now.

longlivets.com
why: Timely folklore did-you-know riding the 'salt-air month' fan ritual peaking this week (see today's listening scan: Swifties are re-streaming 'august' and calling August 'salt air month'). Strong why-now hook while staying in warm song-craft lore. Every claim traces to the Vault folklore item 'august, and the girl Taylor says might be named Augusta. Or Augustine.' (sourced Wikipedia 'August (Taylor Swift song)'): the unnamed third narrator of the cardigan/august/betty love triangle, Taylor musing 'Augusta or Augustine' in the Long Pond Sessions, written+produced with Jack Antonoff, Hot 100 debut at No. 23 in the opening week, the full-orchestra major-chord outro, and Rob Sheffield's 2021 Rolling Stone catalog ranking (5th, 'the album's most plainly beautiful ballad'). 'salt air' is a real lyric from the song. Song-craft lore only -- outside every #36/Clownbot blocklist topic. Media: /eras/folklore.png (committed, deployed era tile).
